Meir Orbach 15:00, 24.11.26 Cybersecurity company Dante Security, which has developed a platform for monitoring the activity of AI agents within organizations, has raised $10 million in a Seed funding round. The round was led by NFX, with participation from Alpha Drive, Inovia and other private investors. Full list of Israeli high-tech funding rounds in 2026 Dante was founded less than a year ago by Moshe Lipsker, formerly general manager of Imperva’s Israeli operations and the company’s global head of R&D; Gabi Beyo, previously a development manager in Imperva’s innovation department; and serial entrepreneur Shai Feinberg. Lipsker is also a colonel in the reserves. He and Feinberg first met while serving together in the Golani Reconnaissance Unit (Sayeret Golani). 1 View gallery Dante Security founders. ( Photo: Victor Levy ) As organizations assign an increasing number of tasks to AI agents, they are granting them access to critical systems and sensitive data, along with permissions that allow them to act autonomously on behalf of employees. Because these agents use valid credentials, even potentially dangerous actions can appear legitimate and evade detection by existing security systems. Related articles: Israeli startup raises $11 million Seed to automate the growing burden of AI security Ramon.Space raises $124 million to build the computing infrastructure of space Israeli startup Newsbound raises $3 million to take on the PR agency model Dante’s platform enables organizations to monitor agent activity from end to end, understand how agents use the access they have been granted, and trace each agent’s actions back to the employee responsible for it. The company aims to help organizations expand their use of AI while maintaining data security, ensuring regulatory compliance and controlling costs. “For decades, the world of cybersecurity has focused on the question of whom to entrust with the keys to an organization’s systems. With the advent of artificial intelligence, we are now entrusting these keys to AI agents that operate autonomously,” said Moshe Lipsker, founder and CEO of Dante Security. “While these agents function within the scope of their assigned permissions, they can still be influenced by malicious instructions to carry out dangerous actions. Traditional security mechanisms remain essential, yet they are not always capable of determining whether such actions are legitimate. Therefore, human oversight is required, bridging these security mechanisms and providing the necessary situational awareness, context and judgment.” TAGS: Dante Security Funding Cybersecurity TAGS Dante Security Funding Cybersecurity Contact Us Newsletter Facebook Twitter About CTech Terms of Use Privacy Policy Dubai Flights Developed by UI & UX by Basch_Interactive
